punchline: Clear's habit trick is to make the first step so small it feels silly: tie the shoes, read one page.
thirty_sec: James Clear's Two-Minute Rule says a new habit should take under two minutes to start. Running becomes tying your shoes, reading becomes one page, yoga becomes taking out the mat. The hard part is starting, and once you've started, continuing is easier. The point isn't to stay at two minutes forever. It's to make showing up a habit before you try to improve it.
